question.text: The bob of a pendulum of mass $m$, suspended by an inextensible string of length $L$ as shown in the figure carries a small charge $a$. An infinite horizontal plane conductor with uniform surface charge density $\sigma$ is placed below it. What will be the time period of the pendulum for small amplitude oscillations?

solution.text: $\therefore$ Apparent weight of the bob, $w^{\prime}=m g-q E$ $$ m y^{\prime}=m g-q E $$ $\therefore$ $g^{\prime}=g-\frac{q E}{m}$ Time period of a pendulum. $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g_{e f f}}}$ $=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g-\frac{q E}{m}}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{\left(g-\frac{q \sigma}{\varepsilon_{0} m}\right)}}$
